causalModel.founding: Argonians die in the Rose. Their bones must reach the dirt. The Chainbreakers built a station near the Blackrose road to receive the bones. The station stands 189 m from the Prison road and not on it.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The station stands on a dry rise. The rise lies between the Prison road and the tracks east to the villages. The Rose's people hand a body to the villages' people there.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The Rose's families release the dead at the station for a fee. The families call the fee a carriage charge. The Chainbreakers pay the fee and record every payment.
causalModel.pressures: The fee is the most resented transaction in the south. Both sides need the fee to continue.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the Rose refused to release the dead, the arrangement would end. The refusal would put the Chainbreakers and the families in open conflict.

districts.notes: A thatched handover shelter on a low dry rise, with the keeper's hut beside it and a way leaving on each side.

why.what: The district is the rise, the handover shelter on it and the keeper's hut.
why.whyHere: The rise lies between the Prison road and the tracks east to the villages. Both parties can reach the rise without entering the other's ground.
why.whySpot: The shelter stands on the flattest part of the rise. The builders levelled the ground under the shelter.
why.whyNeighbours: Blackrose stands about 300 m north-west of the rise, measured at 275 m. The Rose, Blackrose Prison, stands about 500 m west-south-west, measured at 521 m. The ferry stage lies 94 m away. The bonded stores lie 180 m away.
why.playerPurpose: The rise serves the handover of the dead, the fee and the record of the fee.
why.microGeography: The ground is firm and gently sloping grassland. The ground is drier than the marsh to the west.

parcels.orientationWhy: The shelter's open front faces north onto the two ways. The two ways end at the shelter's two front corners. The Rose's way ends at the west corner. The villages' way ends at the east corner.

why.what: The handover shelter is a thatched half pavilion on log posts. The shelter is open at the front.
why.whyHere: The dead change hands under one roof. Both parties stand in sight of each other.
why.whySpot: The shelter stands on a pad of levelled earth at the top of the rise.
why.whyNeighbours: The keeper's hut stands a short walk east of the shelter. The hut stands on the villages' side.
why.playerPurpose: The shelter receives the Rose's dead. The keeper tags the dead and wraps them for the road home.
why.microGeography: Trodden earth lies under the thatch. A row of candles crosses the floor between the two halves.

playerPurpose.note: The handover of the Rose's dead, the tags and the wrapping for the road home.
The procession bearing the dead from the prison ruin stops at the shelter.

parcels.orientationWhy: The keeper's hut door faces south-west. The door faces toward the shelter and the way to it.

why.what: The keeper's hut is a bamboo store hut on short stilts. The Chainbreakers' keeper holds the carriers' stores there. The keeper writes down every fee paid.
why.whyHere: The hut stands on the villages' side of the shelter. The villages' side is the Chainbreakers' charge.
why.whySpot: The hut stands on a levelled pad north-east of the shelter. The pad lies above the villages' way.
why.whyNeighbours: The shelter is a short walk south-west of the hut. The track east starts below the hut door.
why.playerPurpose: The hut holds the keeper, the ledger of carriage charges and the carriers' stores.
why.microGeography: The hut is bamboo on a mud pad. A wicker table and chairs stand outside the door.

playerPurpose.note: The keeper's ledger of carriage charges, kept at the table by the door: every fee paid at the shelter, by date, name and amount.
The Chainbreakers' stores for the carriers: barrels, dried fish and wine.
A quest asks the player to check the ledger of carriage charges.

routes.why: The villages' way is the end of the track from the villages. The way runs on past the keeper's hut to the east corner of the shelter.
The keeper's path is a short path up from the villages' way to the keeper's door.
The Rose's porters use the Rose's way. The way runs from the shelter's west corner down the slope toward the Prison road.

questSockets.why: The procession for the dead of White Rose Prison stops at the shelter. The bones change hands there before the road home.

approaches.sequence: A traveller comes west along the track from the villages. The keeper's hut shows first on the rise, then is hidden by the slope. The thatch of the shelter then appears beyond the hut, with the candles under it.
approaches.wayfinding: The track ends below the keeper's door. The shelter stands a short walk west.

approaches.sequence: A traveller comes off the Prison road across the grass. The shelter's thatch shows on the rise, then the way. The brazier and the bench then show at the shelter's west corner.
approaches.wayfinding: A worn way climbs from the north-west to the shelter's west corner.

networkTerminals.why: The track from the villages to the east ends below the keeper's door.

combatSpaces.why: Open grass surrounds the shelter and the hut on all sides.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The catalogue record The Tag House is a bone-repatriation waystation of magnitude M1 with one door. The lore source is world/sources/lore/topics/prisons.md. White Rose: Argonian bones in stone prisons must be brought to the dirt.
scaleGrounding.why: The tag-keeper works and sleeps at the shelter. The tag-keeper keeps the stores in the hut. The Rose's porters and the villages' carriers come and go.

candidates.why: The chosen candidate is the plotted anchor's own rise. The rise is dry firm ground 3 m above the water table. The place's track from the villages already ends there. The rise has room on its west side for a way down toward the Prison road.
The rejected candidate is the record's near point. The point lies beside the Rose causeway south of Blackrose.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The point lies inside the Blackrose disc after the 2026-09-20 island reseat. The record was moved to the rise.
